mainTopic: The אב's power to annul alone after the ארוס dies, and when the בעל annuls a בוגרת's vows
overview: The גמרא finishes a derivation: the פסוק links vows made before a second betrothal to vows made before a first betrothal. So after the ארוס dies, the אב annuls his daughter's vows alone. It asks whether this covers only vows the ארוס never knew about. It answers that those vows are already learned from 'בנעוריה בית אביה', so the link must also cover vows he did know about. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's line comparing the power of the אב and the בעל, and asks when a בעל annuls the vows of a בוגרת. A girl betrothed as a נערה who then grew up does not work, because בגרות is like the father's death, which does not hand his authority to the ארוס. So the case must be a woman betrothed when already a בוגרת. The גמרא objects that a later משנה already teaches this, and along the way it fixes that משנה's wording to read as two cases. It ends with two answers: either our משנה is the main source, or the later משנה is, and ours repeats it only to match its two 'בזה' clauses.

steps.title: Second betrothal is compared to the first
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares vows made before a second betrothal to vows made before a first betrothal. In both cases the אב annuls alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק compares vows made before her second betrothal to vows made before her first betrothal. Just as the father annuls the first kind on his own, he also annuls the second kind on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes reading a פסוק. It uses a comparison (הקש) to show that after the ארוס dies, the אב goes back to annulling his daughter's vows by himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before her first betrothal, only the אב can annul her vows. The פסוק places the two betrothals side by side. So once the ארוס dies and she has not yet married again, the אב again has full power alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares or links; the פסוק sets two cases side by side so they share the same law (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
Literally 'being'; here it means being betrothed to a man
Annuls (a vow)
By himself, alone

phrases.english: It compares [vows] preceding the second 'being'
phrases.notes: 'Being' here means getting betrothed. The doubled wording 'היו תהיה' in במדבר 30:7 hints at two betrothals.

phrases.english: to [vows] preceding the first 'being'.
Just as with [vows] preceding the first 'being'
the father annuls on his own,
so too with [vows] preceding the second 'being'
the father annuls on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַקִּישׁ קוֹדְמֵי הֲוָיָה שְׁנִיָּה לְקוֹדְמֵי הֲוָיָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation from the earlier part of the daf about the double wording of 'being' in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the ארוס dies, the אב annuls his daughter's vows alone, just as before her first betrothal.

steps.title: Maybe this only covers vows the ארוס never knew about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests limiting the rule: maybe the אב annuls alone only for vows the ארוס never heard of, but not for vows he did hear of.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe this rule applies only to vows the betrothed man never found out about. But for vows he did find out about, the father cannot annul alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the rule from Step 1. It suggests a narrower reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ארוס heard the vow and had a chance to act on it, maybe that vow is already 'his'. Then the אב alone could not annul it after the ארוס dies. This attack tries to shrink the reach of the הקש.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / maybe; introduces a suggested alternative reading
This applies only to...
Literally 'were seen'; here, came to the man's knowledge
Betrothed man (after קידושין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: Say that this applies only
to vows that were not seen by the betrothed man.
phrases.notes: 'Not seen' means he never heard of them, so he never had a chance to cancel or keep them.

phrases.english: but with vows that were seen by the betrothed man
the father cannot annul [them]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the rule from Step 1 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the הקש in Step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Suggests the הקש only covers vows the ארוס never knew about, which would leave the אב powerless alone over vows the ארוס did know about.

steps.title: Those vows are already covered by another פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that vows the ארוס never knew about are already covered by 'בנעוריה בית אביה'. So the הקש must teach something new: even vows he did know about.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were only about vows the betrothed man never found out about, we would already know that from the words 'in her youth, in her father's house'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The narrow reading would make the הקש teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בנעוריה בית אביה' already teach that the אב controls vows made while she is in his house. A פסוק would not need to repeat that. So the הקש must add something: the אב alone annuls even vows that came to the ארוס's knowledge before he died.

keyTerms.meaning: If
It comes out / is learned from
'In her youth, in her father's house' — the פסוק giving the אב power over her vows

steps.whatToRemember: After the ארוס dies, the אב alone annuls his daughter's vows. This holds even for vows the ארוס knew about, because a separate פסוק already covers the ones he didn't know about.

phrases.english: If [it were only] about vows not seen by the betrothed man
that is learned from 'in her youth, in her father's house'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limitation suggested in Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redundancy argument: the narrow reading would make the הקש unnecessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הקש might only cover vows the ארוס never knew about.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הקש covers even vows the ארוס knew about, since the unknown ones are already learned from 'בנעוריה בית אביה'.

steps.title: New line of the משנה: where each one's power is greater
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה saying the אב's power is greater than the בעל's in one way. It then asks what case the משנה has in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: in this matter the father's power is greater than the husband's, etc. The גמרא asks: what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for the exact case. This is a setup; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה line: in another way the בעל's power is greater, because he can annul even after she is a בוגרת. The גמרא wants to know what situation that describes.

keyTerms.meaning: The power is stronger / greater
Husband
What is the case? How does it look?
Etc. — the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: In this the power of the father is greater
than the power of the husband, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: in another way the husband is stronger, since he can annul even after she reaches adulthood.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּזֶה יִפָּה כֹּחַ הָאָב מִכֹּחַ הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case in which the בעל annuls the vows of an adult (בוגרת) wife, as the משנה describes.

steps.title: First suggestion: betrothed as a young girl, then she grew up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה means a girl betrothed while a נערה who later became a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the case is that he betrothed her when she was a נערה, and then she became a בוגרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer to the question from step 4. It is testing this answer, and the next step will knock it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that once she grows up, the father loses his rights over her vows. Maybe the ארוס then takes over and can annul by himself. The word אילימא tells us this suggestion is about to be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (opens a suggestion that will be rejected)
A girl in the stage just after age 12, still under her father's authority
And she grew up (became a בוגרת)

phrases.english: If you say that he betrothed her when she was a young girl,
and then she became a grown woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question היכי דמי from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of בגרות lets the בעל annul alone
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Betrothed as a נערה and then she matured

steps.title: Problem: growing up is like the father dying
steps.stepSummary: Both the father's death and בגרות remove her from the אב's authority. Since death does not pass the authority to the ארוס, בגרות does not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, death takes her out of the father's authority, and growing up takes her out of the father's authority. Just as with death the authority does not pass over to the בעל, so too with בגרות the authority does not pass over to the בעל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion by comparing it to the case of the father's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that when the אב dies, the ארוס does not get the father's share and cannot annul alone. בגרות ends the father's authority in the same way, so it should work the same. So in this case the ארוס cannot annul alone either, and the משנה cannot be talking about it.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, since (introduces an obvious premise)
The stage of full adulthood (six months after נערות)
The father's authority over his daughter
Was emptied over, passed fully over

phrases.english: After all, death takes her out,
and growing up takes her out of the father's authority.

phrases.aramaic: מָה מִיתָה — לֹא נִתְרוֹקְנָה רְשׁוּת לַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: Just as with death, the authority does not pass over to the husband,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בַּגְרוּת — לֹא נִתְרוֹקְנָה רְשׁוּת לַבַּעַל!
phrases.english: so too with growing up, the authority does not pass over to the husband!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The case of betrothal as a נערה followed by בגרות
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בגרות is like the father's death, and death does not hand the father's authority to the ארוס

steps.title: Second suggestion: betrothed when already grown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now says the משנה means a woman betrothed when she was already a בוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he betrothed her when she was already a בוגרת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first answer failed, the גמרא gives a new answer to the question of step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the father never had authority over her vows during the betrothal, since she was already grown. So the בעל alone is the one with power over her vows. This answer works on its own, but the next step will raise a different problem with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (replaces a rejected answer)
A fully grown woman, no longer under her father

phrases.english: Rather, he betrothed her when she was already a grown woman —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of בגרות lets the בעל annul alone
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She was betrothed when already a בוגרת

steps.title: Problem: a later משנה already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: If that is the case, the משנה is repeating something taught in another משנה about a בוגרת who waited twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we already learned this once: 'A בוגרת who waited twelve months.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer: why would the משנה teach a rule that another משנה already teaches?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later משנה (73b) discusses a בוגרת whose ארוס must already support her, and רבי אליעזר says he can annul her vows alone. So a בוגרת whose בעל annuls is already covered there. Teaching it twice looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: One time, already once
Who waited

phrases.english: But we already learned this once:
'A grown woman who waited twelve months'?
phrases.notes: This is a later משנה on 73b, where she waited after the betrothal and the ארוס now has to support her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 7 for making the משנה repeat itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה means a woman betrothed as a בוגרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should not teach something already taught in another משנה

steps.title: Side problem: why twelve months for a grown woman?
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה itself is hard: a בוגרת only needs thirty days to prepare for marriage, not twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: This line itself is difficult. You said: 'A בוגרת who waited twelve months.' Why do I need twelve months for a בוגרת? Thirty days are enough for a בוגרת!
steps.whatsHappening: Before finishing the main problem, the גמרא stops to question the wording of the משנה it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiting time is for preparing for the wedding. A נערה gets twelve months, but a בוגרת gets only thirty days. So the words 'a בוגרת who waited twelve months' do not seem to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult (a problem inside the quoted text)
It is enough for her

steps.confusionAlert: This is a side question about the other משנה. The main problem from step 8 is still open, and the גמרא comes back to it in step 11.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ הַבּוֹגֶרֶת שֶׁשָּׁהֲתָה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: you said, 'A grown woman who waited twelve months,'

phrases.aramaic: בְּבוֹגֶרֶת לְמָה לִי שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ?
phrases.english: why do I need twelve months for a grown woman?
For a grown woman, thirty days are enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side question about the משנה quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'הבוגרת ששהתה שנים עשר חדש'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בוגרת only gets thirty days to prepare, so twelve months does not fit her

steps.title: Fix: read it as two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: Read the משנה as 'a בוגרת, and a girl who waited twelve months', meaning two different cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it this way: 'A בוגרת, and one who waited twelve months.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the later משנה so that it makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the word 'and' splits the line into two cases. The בוגרת waits thirty days, and the twelve months belongs to a נערה. This settles the side question.

phrases.english: Teach it as: 'A grown woman,'
'and one who waited twelve months.'
phrases.notes: This second case is a נערה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי: בּוֹגֶרֶת, וְשֶׁשָּׁהֲתָה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives a בוגרת twelve months
steps.terutzMaskana: It lists two cases: a בוגרת with thirty days and a נערה with twelve months

steps.title: Back to the main problem: it is still a repetition
steps.stepSummary: Even after fixing the wording, the later משנה still mentions a בוגרת, so our משנה still seems to repeat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is still difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main problem from step 8, which the side discussion did not solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fix in step 10 explained the twelve months, but the later משנה still talks about a בוגרת whose ארוס can annul. So we still need to explain why both משניות teach it. Steps 12 and 13 give two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, either way

phrases.english: In any case, it is still difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and restates the problem of step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two משניות still seem to teach the same rule about a בוגרת

steps.title: Our משנה is the main source, the other sets up a מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה is where the rule is really taught. The later משנה mentions a בוגרת only to show the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this: here it is meant exactly, and there it mentions a בוגרת because it wants to show how רבי אליעזר and the רבנן disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the repetition problem and keeps the answer of step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real repetition, because each משנה has its own purpose. Our משנה is the main place for this rule. The later משנה brings up a בוגרת only as part of the case where רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (offers an answer)
Exactly, meant precisely
To show a disagreement

steps.whatToRemember: The בעל annuls alone during בגרות only when he betrothed her as a בוגרת. If she was betrothed as a נערה and then grew up, בגרות works like the father's death, and the ארוס does not take over. This step's answer is that our משנה is the main source. The next step gives a second answer that reverses this.

phrases.english: If you want, say: here it is meant exactly,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our משנה. It is the real source of the rule.

phrases.english: and it mentions a grown woman there
because it wants to show a disagreement
between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repetition problem of steps 8 and 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each משנה has a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות teach the same rule for no reason
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is the main source, and the later one mentions a בוגרת only to present the מחלוקת
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of the משנה is a woman betrothed when she was already a בוגרת

steps.title: The other משנה is the real source, and ours repeats it for style
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the משנה about the בוגרת is where the rule is really taught. Our משנה repeats it only because its first clause opened with "בזה" ("in this"), so it opened the second clause with "בזה" too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this instead: the משנה about the בוגרת is the real source of the rule. Our משנה only repeats it because it said "in this" in the first part, so it said "in this" in the second part too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question of why our משנה repeats a rule about the בוגרת. It says the other משנה is the real teacher of the rule, and our משנה mentions it only to match its own wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the גמרא said our משנה is the main source, and the other משנה only mentions the בוגרת to show the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן. Here it says the reverse: the other משנה is the true source. Our משנה said "בזה יפה כח האב מכח הבעל" ("in this the father's power is greater than the husband's") in its first clause. So it matched it with a second "בזה" clause, where the husband's power is greater, even though that rule is not new.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you wish, say": introduces a second, different answer
Precisely, really; here it marks the משנה that is the true source of the rule
Since it already used, or because it took; explains why something was said just for balance
The first clause of a משנה
The later clause of a משנה
"In this": the opening word of both clauses of our משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to answer the repetition question: (1) our משנה is the source and the other משנה mentions the בוגרת for the מחלוקת, or (2) the other משנה is the source and our משנה repeats it only so its two "בזה" clauses match.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not cancel the rule that a husband can cancel a בוגרת's נדרים. Both answers agree on the rule. They only argue about which משנה is really the one teaching it.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
[The mishna of] "a grown woman" is meant exactly.
phrases.notes: This is the other משנה, the one that mentions a בוגרת and a girl who waited twelve months.

phrases.english: And since it used "in this" in the first clause
phrases.notes: The first clause says: in this, the father's power is greater than the husband's.

phrases.english: It used "in this" in the later clause as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the repetition problem from steps 8 and 11. It reverses step 12's view of which משנה is the main source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the repeated clause in our משנה is there only to balance the wording, not to teach something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to be teaching, for no reason, a rule already taught in the other משנה about the בוגרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The other משנה really teaches the rule. Our משנה repeats it only so its second "בזה" clause matches the first.
